article.content: Chancellor warns of ‘global economic storms’ threatening UK economy Budget 2026: key points at a glance Martin Lewis said that, when he met John Healey this morning, the chancellor said that, having removed standing charges from gas bills, he would also like to get rid of them from electricity bills. Lewis said: The chancellor said he will be talking to Ofgem about how they get rid of the charge on electricity as well, but that is ‘trickier’ apparently and will take longer. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
Millions of households across the United Kingdom are set to receive a **£100 energy payment**, according to an announcement made by Chancellor **John Healey** during the latest fiscal address. Delivering the government's financial plans, Healey pointed to looming international financial turbulence as a primary threat to domestic stability, warning lawmakers about severe "global economic storms" currently buffeting the country. The newly unveiled package also builds on prior policy shifts, with the chancellor indicating an ambition to address utility billing structures following the removal of standard gas fees.

Consumer champion **Martin Lewis** revealed details of his morning consultation with the chancellor, confirming the ongoing discussions regarding household utility overheads. According to Business | The Guardian, these measures form part of a broader strategy aimed at shielding consumers from escalating utility costs during a period of macroeconomic uncertainty. Prior to these announcements, the administration had already rolled out targeted measures, as detailed in our analysis of [Healey vows cheaper marmalade and gherkins in pre-Budget package of 'everyday fixes'](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/healey-vows-cheaper-marmalade-and-gherkins-in-pre-budget-package-of-everyday), focusing on everyday retail items to ease cost-of-living pressures.

British fiscal policy has historically balanced central taxation adjustments with targeted cost-of-living interventions, particularly as global energy markets experience extreme volatility. Administrations frequently deploy direct household support mechanisms when international supply chains face disruption, aiming to protect low-income consumers from volatile market spikes. Readers seeking a broader perspective on the underlying economic pressures can review our report on [Budget 2026: six charts that reveal the economic realities facing the chancellor](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/budget-six-charts-that-reveal-the-economic-realities-facing-the-chancellor).

## Why This Matters

For millions of British families grappling with persistent inflation and high utility overheads, direct financial interventions represent a vital lifeline against fuel poverty. The stakes are particularly high for vulnerable demographics who allocate a disproportionate share of their disposable income to basic heating and electricity needs. When international commodity prices surge, household budgets absorb immediate shocks, making government-backed rebates or structural fee removals critical for maintaining basic living standards.

## What to Watch

Observers will monitor the mechanics of the £100 disbursement to see how efficiently funds reach qualifying accounts ahead of peak winter demand. Analysts are also watching for any subsequent policy adjustments regarding remaining utility standing charges and how the Treasury plans to offset these expenditures amidst wider economic headwinds.

Sources: [Business | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/live/2026/oct/28/budget-2026-latest-updates-john-healey-andy-burnham-labour-uk-politics)
